1. Under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. the BLAPL has been filed by the petitioner in jail custody in connection with Attabira P.S. Case No. 217 of 2023 corresponding to C.T. Case No. No.31 of 2023 pending in the court of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge under POCSO Act,
Bargarh for alleged commission of offence under Sections 376(3) of IPC read with Section 4 of POCSO Act.

Since the earlier BLAPL No.1752 of 2024 filed by the petitioner was disposed of by this Bench by order dated 06.05.2024, the present petition has been placed before this Bench for consideration of renewed prayer for bail in terms of Standing Order No.2 of 2023 dated 21.05.2023.

3. Pursuant to the order dated 29.11.2024, 06.12.2024, the informant/victim having been intimated regarding their right of audience in the present proceeding in response to the prayer for bail of the petitioner who is accused.
The informant along with the learned counsel Mr. Sahoo are present at the virtual Court, High Court of Orissa, Bargarh.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner reiterates his submissions for grant of bail for the fact that the petitioner is in jail custody since 07.06.2023.
Though the trial has progressed, out of 29 witnesses 11 witnesses have been examined and the trial is likely to continue for a further period.

5. In response to the order of this Court dated 23.12.2024 the learned ADJ-cum-P.O., Special Court under POCSO Act, Bargarh by letter dated 08.01.2025 has intimated that out of 29 charge-sheeted witnesses, 20 number of witnesses have already been examined including the victim and her parents and the case stands posted to 15.01.2025 for examination of other witnesses.
It has been further indicated that further about one month time would be necessary from the next date of posting for completion of the trial.

6. The learned Additional Government Advocate referring to the materials on record as well as the earlier order passed by this Court rejecting the prayer for bail dated 06.05.2024 in BLAPL No.1752 of 2024 opposes the prayer for bail.
Learned counsel for the informant opposes the prayer for bail referring to the earlier order dated 06.05.2024 rejecting the prayer for bail.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Additional Government Advocate and the learned legal aid defence counsel for the informant/victim, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the petitioner as there are no reasons/changed circumstances to take a different view from earlier order rejecting the prayer for bail.
8. The BLAPL stands disposed of.

9. However, before parting with the matter considering the status of trial as indicated in the report received from the learned court in seisin of the matter, it is directed that steps be taken for expeditious completion of trial, preferably by 31st March, 2025.
The prosecution as well as the defence are directed to cooperate in completion of trial expeditiously.
The registry shall communicate this order to the learned court in seisin of the matter.
